items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So we ended up playing together. From then on, she said wow. So we’ve done gigs. We did The Anthology down there in San Diego, and we did Yakima, Washington. We did UCLA twice, and we did the Grammy museum.

ctx.x: nights, but not the same nights. So she invited me to play with them the night before we left. I sat in, played a couple of tunes with them, which she loves, because she likes that combination, flute and vocal. Kenny Burrell was responsible for us meeting, in the sense that he had me come play a duet for the Grammy pre- – Grammy museum, pre-Grammy awards, two years ago. That’s when she was there with Alan Bergman. You know the guy?

She was doing one of Michel Legrand’s tunes. I said, “Boy, that would be nice. Let me sit in with you guys.” She said, “Oh yeah.” So we ended up playing together. From then on, she said wow. So we’ve done gigs. We did The Anthology down there in San Diego, and we did Yakima, Washington. We did UCLA twice, and we did the Grammy museum. So we’re already playing. Now we’re getting ready to do Tempe, Arizona, on the – yeah, like I told you, that conflict I had. That is going to be on the 15th of April.
